name: T-cell Immunodeficiency with Epidermodysplasia Verruciformis

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, widespread, flat wart-like or pityriasis versicolor-like skin lesions characteristic of epidermodysplasia verruciformis
Demonstrated T-cell immunodeficiency evidenced by decreased T-cell counts or impaired T-cell function
Detection of beta-human papillomavirus types 5 or 8 in skin lesions by PCR or immunohistochemistry
Family history of epidermodysplasia verruciformis or immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic EV skin lesions plus documented T-cell immunodeficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by immunological and virological testing; genetic testing may identify underlying mutations.

pathognomonic.notes: Lesions resemble pityriasis versicolor or plane warts, typically on sun-exposed areas
searchTerms: flat wart skin lesions that don't go away

pathognomonic.symptomName: T-cell lymphopenia or functional T-cell defects
pathognomonic.notes: Reduced CD4+ and/or CD8+ T-cell counts or impaired proliferation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic beta-HPV infection of skin lesions
searchTerms: long-term wart virus infection on skin
persistent beta human papillomavirus skin lesions

common.symptomName: Increased susceptibility to cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
common.notes: Malignant transformation of EV lesions, especially in sun-exposed skin
searchTerms: higher risk of skin squamous cell cancer

common.notes: Secondary bacterial or fungal infections of skin lesions
searchTerms: skin infections that keep coming back

common.notes: Exacerbation of lesions with sun exposure

occasional.notes: Candida infections of skin and mucous membranes
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

occasional.notes: Thickened, brittle nails associated with chronic skin disease

rare.notes: Rare CNS infections due to immunodeficiency

searchTerms: intense viral infections affecting multiple organs

laboratory: Reduced CD4+ and/or CD8+ T-cell counts
Detection of beta-HPV DNA in skin lesions by PCR
imaging: Imaging generally not diagnostic; may be used to evaluate suspected malignancies
other: Histopathology of skin lesions showing characteristic EV changes

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily genetic defect in skin susceptibility without systemic immunodeficiency
Profound combined T- and B-cell immunodeficiency
Early severe infections beyond skin involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of cutaneous lesions to squamous cell carcinoma
Marked lymphopenia or profound T-cell dysfunction
references: Orth G. Epidermodysplasia verruciformis: a model for understanding the role of host genetics in HPV infection. J Clin Virol. 2006.
Ramoz N, Rueda LA, Bouadjar B, et al. Mutations in two adjacent novel genes are associated with epidermodysplasia verruciformis. Nat Genet. 2002.
Wang Z, Wang Y, Li J, et al. T-cell immunodeficiency in epidermodysplasia verruciformis: clinical and immunological features. Clin Immunol. 2018.
